title: Defect-cavity stack with transmission resonance at 1550 nm
scientific_hypothesis: Introducing a half-wave defect cavity layer within a Bragg stack will create a narrow transmission resonance at 1550 nm center wavelength, achieving higher peak transmittance in 1530-1565 nm than a simple periodic stack, while maintaining visible reflection.
design_principle: Defect modes in photonic crystals create localized states within the stopband. By placing a half-wave cavity (optical thickness = λ/2 at 1550 nm) within a Bragg reflector, a transmission peak appears at the cavity wavelength while the surrounding layers maintain visible reflection.
proposed_topology: Air | (hfo2, sio2) x 7 | hfo2(cavity) | (sio2, hfo2) x 7 | sio2 substrate, total 30 layers with one defect layer
design_variables: Bragg pair thicknesses for visible reflection
defect cavity layer thickness for 1550 nm resonance
number of pairs on each side of cavity
soft_objectives: minimize transmission bandwidth to isolate quantum signal
manufacturing_considerations: Defect layer thickness must be controlled to sub-nm precision
Symmetry around cavity affects resonance quality
30 layers total limits the number of Bragg pairs on each side
theory_basis: Defect mode theory in photonic crystals
Transfer matrix method with defect layers
expected_advantages: Higher peak transmittance at target wavelength than broadband designs
Narrow transmission band reduces background noise
known_risks: Narrow transmission may miss parts of 1530-1565 nm band
Defect layer adds complexity to optimization
Visible reflection may be reduced due to fewer Bragg pairs
execution_request_english: Design a 30-layer defect-cavity multilayer coating on SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: 7 pairs of hfo2/SiO2 (Lemarchand) Bragg reflector, followed by one hfo2 cavity layer at half-wave optical thickness for 1550 nm, followed by 7 pairs of SiO2 (Lemarchand)/hfo2 Bragg reflector (reverse order for symmetry), totaling 30 layers. Optimize Bragg pair thicknesses for 400-700 nm reflection and cavity layer thickness for 1550 nm transmission resonance. Use measured refractive index data for hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from the material catalog. Total layer count fixed at 30.
